key_insight: Photoacoustic imaging safely detected meal-related increases in intestinal blood flow in children without changing oxygenation, suggesting a noninvasive way to assess bowel vascular health.
clinical_relevance: This early pediatric study supports photoacoustic imaging as a feasible biomarker tool for monitoring intestinal perfusion, which may aid future evaluation of conditions such as necrotizing enterocolitis.
method: 18 healthy pediatric participants were scanned before and after a lipid-rich snack.
Photoacoustic images were collected in each abdominal quadrant.
Regions of interest were manually drawn to quantify Hb, HbO2, HbT, and sO2.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports only minor temporary adverse events and significant post-prandial increases in intestinal hemoglobin measures, with no change in oxygen saturation.
watch_item: Findings are from a small, healthy pediatric cohort, so performance in ill infants and for real-world clinical decision-making still needs validation.
paper_title: Photoacoustic imaging of intestinal physiological biomarkers in infants and children
